title: Uniform Pluricanonical Iitaka Fibrations
main_claim: For each d there is m(d) such that for every smooth projective d-fold X with kappa(X)>=0 over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, |m(d)K_X| defines the Iitaka fibration, meaning its section ratios generate the full Iitaka field. This is proved together with a uniform index theorem: a(d,Phi)(K_X+B)~0 for every projective lc pair with DCC coefficients and K_X+B~_Q 0.

issues.location: preliminaries.tex Thm good-models; used throughout (scalar.tex reductions, denominators.tex good special-fibre model, completion.tex Lemma all-degree)
issues.description: The whole induction depends on the companion preprint LA (good log minimal models, which includes nonvanishing and abundance, for every lc pair with pseudo-effective adjoint). That is a major open conjecture, and its proof is not in this paper, so the main theorem is only as strong as LA. The same applies to SD (Stein-degree bound, whose statement matches the use in Prop lc-reduction) and to the U4 chain, tracking and covering lemmas (statements checked against U4 and they match). No circular dependence was visible from this paper.
issues.evidence: "We use the good-log-minimal-model theorem of the companion Log abundance in characteristic zero [LA, Theorem 11.1] ... It includes nonvanishing and is used in all dimensions."

issues.location: denominators.tex, Lemma den-characters, nonabelian blocks (good special-fibre model and the fixed-point step)
issues.description: Two steps are only sketched. First, the G-equivariant MMP upstairs is only G-Q-factorial, and the paper asserts that (Y,T) stays dlt, with normal components and at most s+1 components through a point, without a reference that covers the non-Q-factorial setting. Second, the coherent Lefschetz fixed-point theorem is applied to the singular Gorenstein scheme T and justified only by 'equivariant embedding and localization'. Both are very likely true (a free cyclic action gives zero trace by Riemann-Roch for numerically trivial line bundles), but they are not proved in the text.
issues.evidence: "They preserve dlt for the pair with the special fibre added." ; "Its vanishing statement when there are no fixed points applies to the possibly singular projective scheme T, for example by equivariant embedding and coherent Lefschetz localization."

issues.description: The klt-with-boundary case is handed entirely to Xu's Theorem 1.8 (arXiv:1905.00297). I could not check offline that the hypotheses of that theorem are exactly 'K_j for j<=n plus L_j for j<n'.
issues.evidence: "Xu's klt induction theorem [Xu2019, Theorem 1.8] therefore supplies the assertion when (X,B) is klt."

coverage: I read every section in full: introduction, preliminaries, index.tex (vertical descent, lc-reduction via adjunction, residue and Stein-degree norm, finite-character lemma, quasi-étale factor comparison), scalar.tex (structural reductions: product, abelian and single-block cases, terminalization, countable Bir, moving divisors, general-type fibres; small-fibre volume lemma; upper order estimate; thick-fibre lower Seshadri bound), diagonal.tex (truncated-power slopes, flag bound, external-product orders, the full Frobenius rank comparison; transport section: single-slot finiteness, degree bound, constant-run argument, distribution descent, cocycle, flows), denominators.tex (canonical bundle formula, weights, semistable block models, the inertia relation zeta^{b ord a} prod lambda^{p0}=1, abelian Hodge-line eigenvalues, CY/HK trace and fixed-point argument, big-base corollary, rc-torsion via Birkar boundedness and Kummer theory), and completion.tex. I recomputed the following by hand: the mu_max bound 2b0pD+c2, the flag leading term (2b0p)^n H^n, the total rank bound below R/4, the determinant class B/p+((p-1)/2p+lambda_i)K, the order bound below Rtd0 < 3R/4, the a_i congruence bookkeeping (sum equals q=2tr), the volume comparison constant e!/(g!j!), the domination (1+(j+3)m0)K+L, the chain degree bound d_t<=KT^{2n} and the run-length choice of T, and the CY trace 1+(-1)^s lambda^{-1}. I checked the U4 lemma statements (generic chains, chain orders, tracking, covering) and the SD main theorem against how they are used here. I did not audit the LA, R4 or U4 proofs themselves, or the external results of Birkar 2025, Xu 2019 and BZ16 beyond their stated use.
